newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds slip undramatically ahead of U.S data.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds slip undramatically ahead of U.S data.

text.p: Danish bond prices slipped back undramatically in quiet trade on Friday ahead of the afternoon's U.S. jobless, factory goods, leading indicators and NAPM data.
"The American data should liven things up later, in the meantime the market is calm with investors holding off," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was down 0.18 point from the opening at 107.64, yielding 6.85 percent in turnover of only 560 million crowns while its December future rose 0.04 point to 107.14 with 150 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 lost 0.10 point to 85.05.
The crown traded at 3.8399 per mark at 1100 gmt, down from around 3.8380 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 87 during the morning.
